title: I made a deckbuilder with Codex and AI art, what do you think ?
author: FunSlow5534
selftext:
Hey everyone,

Made in Godot with Codex doing a lot of the coding, and AI art.

It runs in your browser, no download: [https://bekri36.itch.io/grimelith](https://bekri36.itch.io/grimelith)

I’m after honest thoughts. What do you think? Did anything confuse you? what can be tweaked added or removed? Even one line helps me a lot.

Thanks a lot for taking the time, and if you’ve got a project of your own, drop the link and I’ll happily try it back!

comments.author: muikrad
comments.body: Based on the screenshot, it's overdone. Too many details and fine lines yet nothing pops out or feels contrasting. It will be branded as classic ai slop. You need simpler lines, more contrast, fewer useless details.

replies.author: samurai_a_cat
replies.body: You should explore the base too. The problem here is not in this at all, but in the contrasts of the scene and the saturation of the plans.

replies.author: FunSlow5534
replies.body: it was  making it hard to work on already, and I was anxious about doing a switch. but am glad I got to hear all of your opinions.

comments.author: Zealousideal-Bar-316
comments.body:
I can see the same problem when we started too. The colors of everthing is to much, if u ask to codex they have 500 pallete colors, a normal with human made are 10-20 colors. We did a AI slop auditor to help us.   
Its not bad, but can see is AI. 

Look this game - https://store.steampowered.com/app/5370000/Ca%C3%A7arola/

Months of evolving and trying to remove AI.

replies.author: Suspicious-Engineer7
replies.body: still looks like ai slop, sorry man

replies.author: Zealousideal-Bar-316
replies.body: Its look, but no like the first version, some parts now are made pra a real human, so, its not more just AI

replies.author: Adevyy
replies.body:
It has some generic elements, but calling that "looks like slop" is a bit of a stretch.

I don't think I'd clock that if I didn't go into the page with the knowledge that it is made with AI.

replies.author: FunSlow5534
replies.body:
Thank you, I honestly though the same. but multiple I couldn't or didn't know how to express this concern to codex. but I'll find a way to work that out. 

Thank you, your feed back is  much appreciated. about your game I'll try to add it to the wish list once I remember  my steam password ahah

comments.author: samurai_a_cat
comments.body: It is worth studying at least the basis of the theory of space perception and stage setting.

replies.author: FunSlow5534
replies.body: Thank you so much, i'll definitely look at that.

replies.author: stanley_ipkiss_d
replies.body: Make your AI agent study it haha

replies.author: samurai_a_cat
replies.body: They know this, just to give them the task of alignment - you need to know that this task needs to be set.

comments.author: FunSlow5534
comments.body: I wanna say thank you to everyone who replied, I honestly didn't expect a single comment. am surprised thank you so much guys.

comments.author: re-skob
comments.body: its the standard ChatGPT Image 2 noise pattern that puts the same level of detail and information in every part of the image, reads like AI slop and basically looks like every game made with AI

comments.author: Ok-Pirate5732
comments.body:
It has way too much stuff going on, which AI tends to do unless you really rein it in. A lot of extra text for no reason, maximalist/clutter in detail and color. And players will notice things like, the railing floating above the floor (is this intentional?), the irregular space between the cards, etc. 

I recommend you don't look at your game for a couple days, then look at it with fresh eyes. Every time I do this I see things that I missed but were actually really obvious

comments.author: AlphabetSoupKitchen
comments.body:
Honest question here: looking at this screenshot, I can identify and recognize all symbology, positioning and conveyed game mechanics via a 1 to 1 mapping to Slay the Spire.

Why would I play this over Slay the Spire? What makes your implementation unique and intriguing? If you have an answer to that, why doesn't it come across in the screenshot?

replies.author: Adevyy
replies.body: I've been looking into marketing-related content lately, and derivative games apparently always struggled from answering that question, even before AI made game dev so accessible. I'd imagine it's even more often now that someone just makes an almost 1-to-1 copy without thinking of "what is the hook of my game that will get people interested?"

replies.author: FunSlow5534
replies.body:
Thank you so much, I like your feed back or rather your way of helping.

Thank you again. I'll try to make something that answers all these questions.

comments.author: oatmellofi
comments.body: just out of curiosity why do all these posts on the sub have 0 upvotes but lots of comments?

replies.author: oatmellofi
replies.body: in terms of the game, balance was way too easy, too much similarity to sts

replies.author: darkoblivion000
replies.body:
Posts that have zero or negative (most likely negative) upvotes will show zero.

So prob means people are giving the post a bet thumbs down

comments.author: Tarl2323
comments.body:
I think it's an fun project. I wouldn't really try to sell it but honestly it makes me want to make my own hobby deck builder. So you've succeeded on that front!

Too much complaint about slop assumes commercial intent. I recently made a clicker slop game as a party invitation.

There's nothing wrong with slop if it's for your personal consumption. Want to put ketchup on your pizza? That's fine, as long as you're the one eating it.

I feel like with AI Slop making a little game is closer to dungeon mastering or the family movie era of camcorders. That's only a good thing. Kids and families deserve creative outlets to make themselves happy.

replies.author: FunSlow5534
replies.body: I made lot's  of slops that were worst than that haha, but since I got this result, I wanted get feedback to make something even better.

replies.body:
I will change that, but for now am just testing. 

there is one or two deck combos  in their that weren't inspired from STS but you need to select them from the deck builder. some were inspired from league of legends passives and skills etc XD but  they aren't accessed by default.

but by default, I just wanted a quick way to test, so STS was an option.

comments.author: dixon_sider
comments.body: It looks too cliche with those cards. Why copy something else so heavily? Have fun with it and play with numbers/mechanics. This looks kinda low effort.

comments.author: YannLeCoomer
comments.body:
People are being dicks this is way less bad than a lot of ai generated art, despite being a bit busy. 

You don’t have to justify the existence of your game either to anyone. I’ll give it a try when I get some downtime tomorrow.

comments.body: Looks like a mix of castlevania and hollow knight, colors seem muted or dull and there is visual detail that doesnt add anything to the gameplay

comments.author: DayCompetitive1106
comments.body: oh another deck building vibecoded slop, thats what i needed

comments.author: PeerieCode
comments.body:
Played it, and I like it. The style is interesting and it has its own vibe. Two things that would help me as a player: the readability could be better, especially hover and highlighting (make it more obvious what I’m pointing at), and I’d love more variety in the cards. Try to find something more specific, unique. Go on with that, you’ve got a good foundation. 

Good luck with it! Since you offered, here’s my project: it’s a small free browser micro-game/survey, no download: [https://pshowo.github.io/first-crew-year/](https://pshowo.github.io/first-crew-year/) Honest thoughts welcome.
